name: Natural Earth
source: https://www.naturalearthdata.com/ (files from https://github.com/nvkelso/natural-earth-vector; raster files from https://naturalearth.s3.amazonaws.com)
credit: Made with Natural Earth. Free vector and raster map data @ naturalearthdata.com.
usedFor: Earth basemap: land, lakes, rivers (1:50m, 1:10m close up), coastlines and present-day country borders (reference only) at 1:110m, 1:50m and 1:10m; today's countries and territories (1:50m) to add to a map; today's states and provinces (admin-1, 1:10m) for the region picker; the land's colours in the satellite look (Natural Earth I land cover, recoloured: data/terrain/earth-cover-4096.webp)
converted: Coordinates rounded to 0.0001 degrees; at 1:10m, land and lakes cut into 10-degree tiles and lines into pieces (for drawing speed); nothing else changed. States and provinces: coordinates rounded to 0.001 degrees; coasts simplified to about 900 m, borders shared between regions kept point for point (scripts/fetch-regions.mjs). Natural Earth I (land cover, version 2.0.0, 16,200 × 8,100 pixels): averaged to 4096 × 2048 cells, recoloured to the colours land has from space and spread over the sea (scripts/fetch-land-cover.mjs).

name: Terrain Tiles (Tilezen, formerly Mapzen)
licence: Open data; each source keeps its own terms (https://github.com/tilezen/joerd/blob/master/docs/attribution.md). At this zoom: ETOPO1 (NOAA) and GMTED2010 (USGS), both public domain.
credit: Global ETOPO1 terrain data U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration; global GMTED2010 terrain data courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey (via the Mapzen terrain tiles).
usedFor: Earth's terrain and sea floor (data/terrain/earth-4096.bin), outside the ice sheets
converted: Resampled from Web Mercator onto a 4096 × 2048 longitude/latitude grid (0.0879° cells, about 9.8 km at the equator) by area-weighted means; rounded to 1 m. Beyond 85.05° the nearest row, smoothed towards the pole.

name: Terrain Tiles, close up (Tilezen, formerly Mapzen)
version: terrarium encoding, zooms 6 to 12, downloaded as needed
licence: Open data; each source keeps its own terms (https://github.com/tilezen/joerd/blob/master/docs/attribution.md): public domain (USGS, NOAA) and open licences with credit (Copernicus EU-DEM, Geoscience Australia, Land Information New Zealand, Kartverket, Natural Resources Canada, INEGI, the UK Environment Agency, Austria's open data, ArcticDEM).
credit: ArcticDEM terrain data DEM(s) were created from DigitalGlobe, Inc., imagery and funded under National Science Foundation awards 1043681, 1559691, and 1542736; Australia terrain data © Commonwealth of Australia (Geoscience Australia) 2017; Austria terrain data © offene Daten Österreichs – Digitales Geländemodell (DGM) Österreich; Canada terrain data contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence – Canada; Europe terrain data produced using Copernicus data and information funded by the European Union - EU-DEM layers; Global ETOPO1 terrain data U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration; Mexico terrain data source: INEGI, Continental relief, 2016; New Zealand terrain data Copyright 2011 Crown copyright (c) Land Information New Zealand and the New Zealand Government (All rights reserved); Norway terrain data © Kartverket; United Kingdom terrain data © Environment Agency copyright and/or database right 2015. All rights reserved; United States 3DEP (formerly NED) and global GMTED2010 and SRTM terrain data courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey.
usedFor: Close in on maps of the Earth with terrain, finer heights (about 40 m to 2.4 km) for the region in view, downloaded when needed through the local data service and kept on this computer (not under the ice sheets, where the bundled grid's ice surface stays); can be turned off per map
converted: Each tile's heights (red × 256 + green + blue / 256 − 32,768 m) laid onto a longitude/latitude grid of the region in view, about as fine as the tiles, by bilinear interpolation (src/terrain/detail.ts).

name: Sentinel-2 cloudless 2016 (EOX)
version: 2016; tiles in longitude and latitude, level 3 bundled, levels 4 to 13 downloaded as needed
credit: Sentinel-2 cloudless - https://s2maps.eu by EOX IT Services GmbH (Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2016 & 2017)
usedFor: The satellite look of maps of the Earth: the planet as photographed. A picture of the whole Earth ships with the app (data/terrain/earth-photo-4096.webp, about 10 km a pixel); close in, the photographs of the region in view (to about 10 m a pixel) are downloaded when needed through the local data service and kept on this computer; can be turned off per map
converted: The bundled picture: the 128 tiles of level 3 laid side by side and saved as WebP (scripts/fetch-earth-photo.mjs). Close in: tiles laid side by side into a picture of the region in view (src/terrain/photo-cache.ts). Colours unchanged; relief shading and the coast of the moment are drawn over them.

sources.file: level 3 tiles (128 JPEG files, in row and column order)

name: Copernicus DEM GLO-90
version: GLO-90 (2021 release), smallest overview of each tile
licence: Free of charge for any use, including commercial, with the credit below (Copernicus DEM licence for GLO-90)
credit: © DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and © Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018 provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA; all rights reserved.
usedFor: The ice surface of Greenland and Antarctica (and the land around Greenland) in data/terrain/earth-4096.bin
converted: Means of the overview pixels (3 to 10 km) in each 0.0879° cell, south of 60° S and within 59°-84° N, 74°-10° W; a cell partly at sea takes the sea floor of the terrain tiles for that part.

name: HYG star database
credit: Star positions: HYG database v4.1 by David Nash (astronexus.com), CC BY-SA 4.0.
usedFor: Space maps of the nearby stars: every star of the database within 50 light-years of the Sun (data/stars/nearby-50ly.json)
converted: Stars within 50 light-years kept; positions turned from parsecs on equatorial axes into light-years on galactic axes and rounded to 0.001 light-years; names made from the proper name, Bayer letter or Flamsteed number with the constellation, or the Gliese, HD or Hipparcos number, and a second name written out ("Epsilon Eridani"); nothing else changed. The converted file is under the same licence (CC BY-SA 4.0).

name: Open Exoplanet Catalogue
credit: Planets of other stars: the Open Exoplanet Catalogue, Hanno Rein and contributors, MIT licence.
usedFor: Known planets of the stars on the nearby star map, in a star's panel and marked on the map (data/stars/exoplanets-50ly.json)
converted: Confirmed planets of systems within 50 light-years whose host star is on the nearby star map (by name, or by its place in the sky and distance); for each its name, period, distance from its star, mass and radius in Earth's, year and way of discovery; nothing else changed. The licence's notice is kept beside the file (data/stars/LICENSE-open-exoplanet-catalogue.txt).

name: PALEOMAP Paleodigital Elevation Models (PaleoDEMs)
source: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5460860 (C. R. Scotese and N. Wright, PALEOMAP Project); resampled to one-degree cells, heights in whole metres (scripts/paleodem-extract.py, scripts/pack-paleodem.ts)
credit: Earth through geological time: PALEOMAP PaleoDEMs, C. R. Scotese and N. Wright (2018), PALEOMAP Project, CC BY 4.0; resampled.
usedFor: The Earth's land and sea floor at 109 moments from today back 540 million years, on maps of the Earth through geological time

name: PALEOMAP plate model (rotations and plate polygons v19o_r1c)
version: v19o_r1c, in PaleoMAP PaleoCoastlines data v7.2 (2023)
source: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7994000 (C. R. Scotese; A. T. Kocsis and C. R. Scotese); the crust's motion between the PaleoDEMs worked out from it (scripts/paleo-motion.py, with pygplates)
credit: Plate motions: PALEOMAP plate model v19o_r1c, C. R. Scotese, from A. T. Kocsis and C. R. Scotese's PaleoMAP PaleoCoastlines data (2023), CC BY 4.0.
usedFor: How the continents move between the PaleoDEMs' moments on maps of the Earth through geological time

name: Natural Earth populated places (1:10m) and countries' populations (1:50m)
credit: Made with Natural Earth. Free vector and raster map data @ naturalearthdata.com.
